references.text: To Adam he said, 'Because you listened to your wife's voice and ate from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you.'
He called his name Noah, saying, 'This one will comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, caused by the ground which the Lord has cursed.'
God saw that the wickedness of man was great on the earth, and that every thought and plan in their hearts was evil continually.
The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence. God looked at the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth.
I establish my covenant with you: Never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.
He shall wash its entrails and its legs with water, and the priest shall burn it all on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me.
For this is like the days of Noah's flood to me: As I swore that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so have I sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick; who can understand it?
For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
And walk in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
Psalm 78:38 explains the merciful dynamic underlying God's promise in Genesis 8:21 not to destroy the earth again.
Genesis 9:15 confirms and reiterates God's promise from 8:21 as part of the formal covenant.
